title: Spatial Clustering of Hepatitis A in South Korea, 2020-2024: Nationwide Bayesian Analysis of Groundwater, Land Cover, and Socioeconomic Gradients (analysis code, data-repair log and compiled data, v2.2.0)
description: Reproducibility package for a Bayesian spatiotemporal analysis of district-level hepatitis A incidence in South Korea, 2020-2024 (negative binomial, Besag-York-Mollie convolution + RW1 + Knorr-Held Type I interaction, fitted with R-INLA; 218 districts, 1,090 district-years, 27 covariates). v2.1.0 is a DATA-REPAIR release that supersedes all earlier versions: an audit found that several administrative source files store unavailable values as 0 instead of missing and that some series were redefined in particular years, so that, under binary and quantile coding, covariates encoded data availability rather than their true level. These values are now recoded as missing and filled from the most recent earlier available year, and every change is logged (results/data_repair_log.csv). The v2.0.x associations for piped water-supply coverage and inpatient medical cost, and the v2.0.x claim of nine credible covariates, were artefacts of this defect and are withdrawn. The repaired analysis found four credible covariates (household groundwater wells, dairy-cattle farms, forest area, fiscal independence). A post hoc extreme-value screen then found aggregation errors (eg, a sex ratio near 50 males per 100 females, basic livelihood security recipients above 30%, mostly in cities with non-autonomous wards) affecting 17 district-years in 4 covariates; v2.2.0 adopts this screen as rule R7 of the principal analysis, which excludes 2 further districts (218 districts, 1,090 district-years) and adds sewer-pipe repair sites as a fifth credible covariate. Household groundwater wells and sewer-pipe repair sites are borderline (lost under some neighbourhood graphs, INLA settings or the alternative handling of extreme values), and only forest area is credible in every sensitivity analysis; dairy-cattle farms, sewer-pipe repair sites and fiscal independence are lost when 2020-2021 is excluded. The covariates take up only part of the spatial structure (residual Moran's I +0.21). The package contains a single R script (data repair, models, sensitivity and stability analyses), a figure script, a year-R2 data-quality screen, the compiled 1,090-row analytic dataset, all result tables, the run log and session information. The covariate specification was developed exploratorily; the reported associations are hypothesis-generating. Releases up to v2.0.6 accompanied an earlier version of the analysis under the title 'Sanitation Infrastructure and Environmental Vulnerability of Hepatitis A Transmission in South Korea, 2020-2024'. v2.1.1 adds a column to results/year_r2_before_after.csv (year-R2 after recovery of the zero-coded values alone) and completes the author affiliations; no change to code logic, data or results. v2.1.2 corrects the description of the inpatient-medical-cost zero counts (documentation only). v2.2.0 adopts the extreme-value screen (rule R7) in the principal analysis, which changes the analytic frame to 218 districts and 1,090 district-years and the credible set to 5 covariates; see the changelog in README.md.
